CMS Program Statistics - Original Medicare Enrollment, Calendar Year 2023
========================================================================

PUBLIC. No DUA, no restriction, no license. Free download from data.cms.gov.

Source file : MDCR ENROLL AB 9-14_CPS_02ENR_2023.zip
Download    : https://data.cms.gov/sites/default/files/2025-09/
              d3e2470b-f7ed-4c92-9615-4bfee94b6bdb/
              MDCR%20ENROLL%20AB%209-14_CPS_02ENR_2023.zip
Retrieved   : 2026-08-29
Publisher   : CMS Office of Enterprise Data and Analytics,
              CMS Chronic Conditions Data Warehouse
Method note : "The enrollment counts are determined using a person-year
              methodology."

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
--------------------
It supplies the ONE quantity the diagnostic denominator table could not
construct: women aged 65+ enrolled in Original Medicare (fee-for-service),
2023. Without it the Medicare FFS rows were NA with missing_reason
`missing_cms_ffs_enrollment_denominator`.

THE FEMALE x 65+ CROSS IS PUBLISHED, NOT IMPUTED
------------------------------------------------
Table 11 gives age and sex only as MARGINALS and cannot supply the cross.
Table 12 ("by Type of Entitlement and Demographic Characteristics") crosses
sex with entitlement type, and "Total Aged" IS the 65+ category -- Table 12
row "65 Years and Over" places its entire count in Total Aged, with zero in
Total Disabled.

Reconciliation, computed rather than asserted:
    Male x Aged      14,290,951
  + Female x Aged    16,542,982
  = 30,833,933  vs published 65+ total 30,833,932  (differs by 1, rounding)

So 16,542,982 is a published cell, not a marginal times a share.

PART A/B CAVEAT -- MATTERS FOR THIS NUMERATOR
---------------------------------------------
16,542,982 counts Part A AND/OR Part B. The numerator (Part B PUF office
visits) requires Part B. Among 65+, Part B coverage is
    25,732,430 / 30,833,932 = 0.83455
but that share is NOT published by sex, so applying it to the female count is
an ASSUMPTION, not a measurement. Both denominators are therefore reported and
the ratio is given both ways rather than picking one silently.
